newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro-bourses fall but largely ignore Deng.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro-bourses fall but largely ignore Deng.

text.p: European markets largely ignored the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping on Thursday, but German shares went into a sharp decline.
The dollar was initially bid up in Europe with Deng's death having a muted impact, but it eased against the mark following publication of a strong business climate report in Germany.
European markets focused mainly on local factors, while Asian investors reacted to Deng's death by marking prices higher in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan.

"It wouldn't be true to say it passed without incident as far as the market was concerned because the dollar did react," said one Zurich-based foreign exchange dealer. "But overall the price action has been slight."
Traders in Europe were more concerned about economic data coming out of Germany, however.
As expected, the German Bundesbank decided to leave interest rates unchanged after releasing money supply data showing strong growth in January.
The country's Ifo economic institute earlier said its west German business climate index jumped to 93.3 in January from 90.9 in December, indicating confidence was growing.
And German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt predicted Europe's largest economy would continue to recover this year.
"We are standing by our forecast of 2.5 percent economic growth," Rexrodt told parliament during a debate of the government's annual economic report.
Despite the bullish sounds from Rexrodt, German shares started trading sharply down, although they later lifted off their lows.
Wall Street's weak performance overnight weighed on the market, while jitters ahead of Friday's expiry of options contracts added to the volatility.
By 1230 GMT, the 30-share DAX index had fallen 1.1 percent to 3,198 points, although government bonds were trading off their lows and the dollar was lending support.

On foreign exchange markets, the dollar was bid up to around 1.7000 marks in early trade before declining to around 1.6876. Against the yen it slipped to 123.54, down almost one yen from late Wednesday's European level.
U.S. January housing starts and weekly jobless claims were due at 1330 GMT, with the February Philadelphia Fed survey following at 1500 GMT.
However, analysts said the big focus for the market was the semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, which U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan will deliver to Congress on February 26 and 27.
The London stock market opened the day showing losses like its main European rivals, but the market later recovered to post a fresh intraday high of 4,362.4.
"We hit a new high, but it didn't feel like it. We're just struggling to maintain these levels," said one dealer.
Dealers said they were awaiting the opening of Wall Street for direction. Government bonds trimmed their opening losses, which helped support shares, dealers said.

Among individual stocks, shares in Reed International Plc jumped 21-1/2p to a four-month high at 1,169 amid persistent market speculation about a bid from Reuters Holdings Plc, dealers said. Reuters shares were up 11p at 677-1/2.
Both companies declined comment on the latest bout of market rumour.
French stocks traded lower through the morning as the market continued to digest its recent gains.
"It's a small consolidation and it's occurring calmly," a trader said. "None of the blue chip CAC issues is losing much more than two percent. It's profit taking affecting the whole of the market."
Although the CAC-40 index was down 19 points at 2,575 by 1230 GMT, traders said the bourse's weakness did not put in doubt the market's broadly rising trend.
Credit Lyonnais certificates shot up nearly seven percent to around 199 francs after Les Echos newspaper said that the state-owned bank expected to report a big increase in profits in 1997.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted as 1.6876 marks and 123.54 yen, compared with 1.6979 marks and 124.35 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 1.1 points, or 0.03 percent, at 4,358.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 18.05 points, or 0.7 percent, at 2,576.71.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 35.59 points, or 1.1 percent, at 3,198.16.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $344.85 against $346.25 on Wednesday. Silver was slightly easier at $5.17.
